name: Hydrogen Peroxide 50% TG

oral_ld50.result: LD50 Rat: 1270 mg/kg (90% solution; equivalent acute toxicity for concentrated H2O2)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue damage. Concentrated solutions (≥50%) are strongly corrosive.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage. Concentrated solutions cause irreversible corneal damage and blindness.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (respiratory tract) through prolonged or repeated inhalation exposure.

persistence: Hydrogen peroxide is readily biodegradable and rapidly decomposes in the environment into water and oxygen. It is not persistent in water, soil, or air. Half-life in water is typically hours to days depending on conditions (light, temperature, catalysts).
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Log Kow = -1.36; BCF is negligible.
mobility: Hydrogen peroxide is highly mobile in aquatic environments and soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc. It rapidly degrades and does not persist in groundwater.
iarc_classification: Group 3 (Not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans)

name: Nitric Acid 37%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue destruction on contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; may cause permanent eye injury.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation and damage following inhalation of vapours; high exposures may cause pulmonary oedema.

persistence: Nitric acid dissociates completely in water to nitrate and hydrogen ions. It is inorganic and not subject to biodegradation. Nitrate is persistent in aquatic environments and does not undergo abiotic degradation under normal conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is inorganic and ionic; bioaccumulation is not expected. BCF is not applicable for inorganic acids.
mobility: Nitric acid is completely miscible with water and dissociates to nitrate ions, which are highly mobile in soil and water environments. Adsorption to soil is negligible.

name: Acetic Acid Glacial

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue destruction on contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; contact may result in corneal injury.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation and damage to mucous membranes upon repeated or prolonged inhalation exposure.

persistence: Acetic acid is readily biodegradable. It is rapidly degraded under aerobic conditions by microorganisms. BOD5/ThOD ratios indicate high biodegradability. It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (-0.17) and high water solubility [BCF: estimated < 10].
mobility: Acetic acid is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low soil adsorption. Koc is estimated at approximately 1 L/kg. Volatilization from water surfaces may occur.

name: Ethaneperoxoic acid

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable in water. 98% degradation in water, measured by DOC removal, after 28 days.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms [BCF: 1.61].
mobility: The substance is highly mobile; therefore, adsorption to soil is not expected (Koc: 1.5 L/kg).

name: Sulfuric Acid 50%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue destruction on contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; contact may result in permanent corneal damage or blindness.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation and damage with repeated or prolonged inhalation exposure. Mists are associated with laryngeal and lung cancer (IARC Group 1 for strong inorganic acid mists containing sulfuric acid).

persistence: Sulfuric acid is an inorganic substance; biodegradation is not applicable. It dissociates in water to hydrogen and sulfate ions. Environmental persistence is assessed in terms of pH effects rather than biodegradation.
bioaccumulation: Sulfuric acid is an inorganic acid that dissociates completely in water. Bioaccumulation is not expected; BCF is not applicable for ionic inorganic substances.
mobility: Sulfuric acid is highly water-soluble and mobile in aquatic environments. It dissociates completely in dilute solution. Koc is not applicable for this inorganic substance.
iarc_classification: Group 1 — Strong inorganic acid mists containing sulfuric acid are classified as carcinogenic to humans (IARC Monograph Vol. 54, 1992). Note: this classification applies to occupational exposure to strong inorganic acid mists, not to sulfuric acid solutions per se.
ntp_classification: Not listed in NTP Report on Carcinogens as a pure substance; strong-acid mists (including sulfuric acid mists) are associated with carcinogenicity per IARC.

regulatory.prop_65_warning: Sulfuric acid (strong inorganic acid mists) is listed under California Proposition 65 as a chemical known to cause cancer.

name: HEDP Liquid Tech Grade 60%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: 1-Hydroxyethylidene-1,1-diphosphonic acid (HEDP) is not readily biodegradable under standard OECD test conditions. It is considered persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: HEDP is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its high water solubility and low log Kow (estimated log Kow < -2). BCF is considered low.
mobility: HEDP is highly water soluble and is expected to be mobile in the aquatic environment. It may adsorb to soils and sediments containing calcium, iron, or aluminum ions, reducing mobility in those media.

name: Sodium Molybdate Dihydrate

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: Repeated or prolonged exposure may cause damage to organs (kidneys, liver) based on animal data.

persistence: Sodium molybdate dihydrate is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It dissociates in water to sodium and molybdate ions. The molybdate ion persists in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Molybdate is an inorganic anion with low bioaccumulation potential.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in aquatic environments as it dissociates into ions. Molybdate may adsorb to soil depending on pH and soil composition.

name: Phosphoric Acid 75%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue damage on prolonged or concentrated contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; concentrated solutions can cause severe burns and permanent injury.

persistence: Phosphoric acid is an inorganic acid and does not undergo biodegradation in the conventional sense. It dissociates in water to phosphate ions, which are naturally occurring nutrients. Persistence as an organic compound is not applicable.
bioaccumulation: Phosphoric acid is an inorganic substance and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms. Bioconcentration factor (BCF) is not applicable.
mobility: Phosphoric acid is highly soluble in water and dissociates to phosphate ions. It is highly mobile in aquatic environments. Sorption to soil is moderate; phosphate can bind to soil particles, limiting leaching in some soils.

name: HPAA Hydroxy Phosphonoacetic Acid 50%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is considered readily biodegradable based on available data. It is not expected to persist in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow and high water solubility.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low adsorption to soil particles.

name: TEA Triethanolamine 85% Solution

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation with prolonged or repeated contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation with repeated or prolonged inhalation exposure.

persistence: Triethanolamine is readily biodegradable. BOD/COD ratios indicate rapid aerobic biodegradation. It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (-1.0). BCF is estimated to be low.
mobility: Triethanolamine is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc. It is expected to leach into groundwater.

name: Sodium Hydroxide 50%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue destruction on contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious irreversible eye damage; risk of blindness on contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause irritation and damage to the respiratory tract upon inhalation of mists or dusts.

persistence: Sodium hydroxide is an inorganic substance and is not subject to biodegradation. It neutralizes in water to form water and sodium salts; persistence as a distinct entity is not applicable. The substance adjusts pH and is rapidly consumed by neutralization reactions in aquatic environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Sodium hydroxide dissociates completely in water into sodium and hydroxide ions; bioaccumulation potential is negligible (BCF not applicable for inorganic ions).
mobility: Sodium hydroxide is highly soluble in water and dissociates completely into ions. In soil, sodium ions are mobile and hydroxide ions are rapidly neutralized. Sorption to soil is not significant (Koc not applicable).

name: Sodium Xylene Sulfonate 40% (SXS-40)

toxicology.skin_result: Mild skin irritant; repeated or prolonged contact may cause irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow and ionic character.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its ionic nature and high water solubility.

name: Sodium Bromide 40% Solution

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: Repeated or prolonged exposure may cause effects on the central nervous system (bromism).

persistence: Sodium bromide is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It persists in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: Sodium bromide is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its ionic nature and low lipophilicity.
mobility: Sodium bromide is highly mobile in soil and water due to its high water solubility and ionic nature.

name: Sodium Tripolyphosphate (STPP)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation with prolonged contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye irritation; may cause eye damage.

persistence: Sodium tripolyphosphate hydrolyzes in water to orthophosphates. It is not considered persistent in the environment; the hydrolysis products (phosphates) are naturally occurring and readily assimilated by organisms.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its ionic nature and high water solubility; log Kow is not applicable for inorganic salts.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in the aquatic environment given its high water solubility; adsorption to soil is limited.

name: Monoethanolamine (MEA)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; corrosive at higher concentrations.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation; STOT single exposure category 3 (respiratory tract irritation).

persistence: Monoethanolamine is readily biodegradable. BOD5/ThOD ratio indicates rapid aerobic degradation in water and soil. It is not expected to be persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (-1.91) and high water solubility. BCF is estimated to be low (BCF < 10).
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc (estimated Koc: 2.3 L/kg). Leaching to groundwater is possible.

name: Potassium Hydroxide 45%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue destruction.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; risk of permanent injury.

persistence: Potassium hydroxide is an inorganic substance; biodegradation is not applicable. It rapidly neutralizes in aqueous environments through acid-base reactions, altering pH. Not subject to abiotic degradation in the conventional sense.
bioaccumulation: Potassium hydroxide is an inorganic ionic compound and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms. Bioconcentration is not applicable.
mobility: Potassium hydroxide is highly soluble in water and highly mobile in the environment. Koc is not applicable for this inorganic electrolyte.

name: NORFOX LDA

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly based on its physicochemical properties.
mobility: The substance is expected to be mobile in soil due to its surfactant properties.

name: Bleach 12.5%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation to severe skin burns depending on concentration and contact duration.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation of vapors or mists.

persistence: Sodium hypochlorite is not persistent in the environment. It rapidly decomposes in water and under sunlight to chloride, oxygen, and hypochlorous acid. It is not considered a persistent substance under OECD criteria.
bioaccumulation: Sodium hypochlorite is not expected to bioaccumulate. The substance is inorganic and dissociates completely in water; BCF is not applicable.
mobility: Sodium hypochlorite is highly mobile in aquatic environments due to its complete dissociation and high water solubility. It rapidly degrades and does not partition significantly to soil (Koc not applicable for inorganic salt).

name: Sodium Metasilicate Anhydrous

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause irritation to the respiratory tract upon inhalation of dust.

persistence: Sodium metasilicate is an inorganic substance; biodegradability is not applicable. In aqueous solution it hydrolyzes to silicic acid and sodium hydroxide. The silicate ion is naturally occurring and does not persist as a hazardous entity.
bioaccumulation: The substance is inorganic and ionic in nature; bioaccumulation is not expected. BCF is not applicable.
mobility: As an inorganic salt that dissociates in water, sodium metasilicate is highly mobile in aquatic environments. Adsorption to soil is expected to be low.

name: Isothiazalone 1.5% (CMIT component)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and is a strong skin sensitizer.

persistence: 5-Chloro-2-methyl-4-isothiazolin-3-one is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. It hydrolyses rapidly in water and is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly. Log Kow is approximately 0.91; BCF estimated < 10.
mobility: The substance has high mobility in soil due to its low Koc (estimated ~15 L/kg) and high water solubility.

name: Methyl Paraben Powder

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: Methyl paraben (CAS 99-76-3) is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. It is expected to be rapidly biodegraded in the environment and is not considered persistent.
bioaccumulation: The substance has a low potential for bioaccumulation (log Kow: 1.96; estimated BCF: ~3.2).
mobility: The substance has moderate mobility in soil (estimated Koc: ~94 L/kg). It may leach into groundwater to some extent.

name: Propyl Paraben Powder

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: Propyl paraben is considered readily biodegradable based on available data.
bioaccumulation: The substance has low bioaccumulation potential (log Kow: 3.04; BCF estimated low).
mobility: Propyl paraben has moderate mobility in soil (log Koc estimated ~2.0).

name: Berol 226 SA Non-ionic Surfactant

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause mild eye irritation; not classified as causing serious eye damage.

persistence: Glycerol is readily biodegradable (>60% BOD in 28 days). It is not persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Glycerol is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow (-1.76) and high water solubility.
mobility: Glycerol is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc.

name: NP-12 Nonylphenol Ethoxylate

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild to moderate skin irritation.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage/severe eye irritation.

persistence: Nonylphenol ethoxylates (NPEOs) are not readily biodegradable under standard aerobic test conditions. They undergo stepwise biodegradation to shorter-chain ethoxylates and ultimately to nonylphenol (NP), which is more persistent. NP and short-chain NPEOs are persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: Nonylphenol ethoxylates have moderate bioaccumulation potential; the parent molecule has a low BCF due to molecular size, but the metabolite nonylphenol has a log Kow of approximately 4.48 and a BCF of approximately 794, indicating the metabolite bioaccumulates.
mobility: The substance has moderate mobility in soil. Log Koc for nonylphenol ethoxylates is estimated at approximately 3.5–4.0, suggesting moderate adsorption to soil and sediment. Degradation products, particularly nonylphenol, are less mobile and bind more strongly to sediment.

name: Glycolic Acid 70% Solution

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation/burns; concentrated solutions (70%) are corrosive to skin.

persistence: Glycolic acid is readily biodegradable. It is expected to biodegrade rapidly in aquatic and soil environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Log Kow is estimated at -1.11, indicating low bioaccumulation potential.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low log Kow.

name: Hydrochloric Acid 35%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation and pulmonary edema at high concentrations.

persistence: Hydrochloric acid dissociates completely in water to hydrogen and chloride ions. Biodegradability is not applicable to inorganic acids. The substance is not persistent in the traditional sense; pH effects are neutralized by buffering capacity of receiving waters.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. As an inorganic acid, bioaccumulation potential is not applicable.
mobility: Highly mobile in aquatic environments. Dissociates completely in water; chloride ions are highly soluble and mobile in soil and groundwater.
iarc_classification: Not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans (IARC Group 3) for hydrochloric acid; strong inorganic acid mists containing sulfuric acid are Group 1, but hydrochloric acid itself is Group 3.

name: Citric Acid Powder Food Grade

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: Citric acid is readily biodegradable (>60% BOD/ThOD in 28 days). It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (-1.72) and high water solubility.
mobility: Citric acid is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc. It is not expected to adsorb significantly to soil or sediment.

name: Urea Bulk

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.

persistence: Urea is readily biodegradable. It is rapidly hydrolyzed in aqueous environments by urease enzymes to ammonia and carbon dioxide. Half-life in water/soil is typically short (days to weeks depending on conditions).
bioaccumulation: Urea is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow (log Kow = -2.11). BCF is negligible.
mobility: Urea is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility (~1080 g/L at 20°C) and low soil adsorption (Koc: approximately 5 L/kg).

name: Sodium Gluconate Granular

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant based on available data.
toxicology.eye_result: Not a serious eye irritant based on available data.

persistence: Sodium gluconate is readily biodegradable. It undergoes rapid aerobic biodegradation in water and soil environments.
bioaccumulation: Sodium gluconate is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow and high water solubility.
mobility: Sodium gluconate is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low adsorption to soil particles.

name: Isopropyl Alcohol 99%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness (STOT-SE Category 3).

persistence: Isopropyl alcohol is readily biodegradable. It is expected to biodegrade rapidly in both aerobic and anaerobic environments. BOD5/ThOD ratio indicates ready biodegradability.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (0.05). BCF is estimated to be low (BCF < 10).
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil and water due to its high water solubility and low Koc (Koc: approximately 1.06 L/kg). It is expected to leach into groundwater.

name: DPA Dipicolinic Acid

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.

persistence: No data available on the biodegradability of dipicolinic acid. The substance is not readily classified based on available information.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow and high water solubility.
mobility: The substance is expected to be highly mobile in soil given its high water solubility and ionizable carboxylic acid groups.

name: Ammonium Sulfate

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation upon prolonged contact.

persistence: Ammonium sulfate is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense. It dissociates in water to ammonium and sulfate ions. Ammonium can be oxidized to nitrate by nitrifying bacteria. The substance is not persistent as an organic compound.
bioaccumulation: Ammonium sulfate is an inorganic ionic compound and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: Ammonium sulfate is highly soluble in water and highly mobile in soil and aquatic environments. The sulfate and ammonium ions readily leach through soil.

name: Ammonium Bifluoride Solid

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue destruction. Fluoride ions penetrate skin causing deep tissue damage and potential systemic toxicity.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage. May cause permanent damage to the cornea and conjunctiva.
toxicology.stot_result: Repeated or prolonged exposure may cause damage to bones and teeth (skeletal fluorosis). May cause damage to kidneys and liver via repeated exposure.

persistence: Ammonium bifluoride is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It dissociates in water to ammonium and bifluoride/fluoride ions. Fluoride ions are persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. As an inorganic ionic compound, bioaccumulation via lipophilic partitioning is not applicable.
mobility: Ammonium bifluoride is highly soluble in water and dissociates completely to ions. Fluoride ions are highly mobile in aquatic and soil environments.

name: Glycol Ether DPM

toxicology.skin_result: Mild skin irritant; repeated or prolonged contact may cause drying and defatting of skin.
toxicology.eye_result: Mild to moderate eye irritant; may cause conjunctival irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness at high concentrations.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. Dipropylene glycol monomethyl ether (DPM) undergoes rapid aerobic biodegradation in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Log Kow is approximately -0.064; low potential for bioaccumulation.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc (estimated ~1–10 L/kg). Leaching to groundwater is possible.

name: Glycol Ether EB

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (blood, liver, kidneys) through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. Biodegradation in water: >60% in 28 days (OECD 301). Not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate (log Kow: 0.83; BCF: estimated <10).
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil (Koc: estimated 1–10 L/kg; log Kow: 0.83). Highly soluble in water.

name: EDTA Tetrasodium

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: Tetrasodium EDTA is not readily biodegradable under standard test conditions. However, it can be biodegraded by adapted microorganisms under certain conditions. It is persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow and ionic nature. BCF is estimated to be low.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its ionic character and high water solubility. Low adsorption to soil is expected.

name: Zinc Chloride 62.5%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue damage. Corrosive to skin.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage. Corrosive to eyes.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation and damage following repeated or prolonged inhalation exposure.

persistence: Zinc chloride is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. Zinc ions persist in the environment and are not degradable. Environmental fate is governed by adsorption, precipitation, and speciation processes.
bioaccumulation: Zinc is an essential element at low concentrations but can bioaccumulate in aquatic organisms at elevated concentrations. BCF values for zinc in fish are generally low (BCF ~100 or less), indicating limited bioaccumulation potential relative to many organic substances.
mobility: Zinc chloride is highly soluble in water and mobile in aquatic environments. Mobility in soil is moderate and depends on pH and soil composition; zinc tends to adsorb to soil particles and organic matter at higher pH.

name: Ethanol 200 Proof SDA 40B

toxicology.skin_result: Not a significant skin irritant at typical exposures; prolonged or repeated contact may cause defatting and mild irritation.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye irritation; vapors may irritate eyes.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness (CNS depression) at high concentrations.

persistence: Ethanol is readily biodegradable. It is rapidly degraded under aerobic conditions with a BOD5/ThOD ratio indicating high biodegradability. Estimated atmospheric half-life is approximately 4 days via reaction with hydroxyl radicals.
bioaccumulation: Ethanol is not expected to bioaccumulate in aquatic organisms (log Kow = -0.31; BCF estimated < 1).
mobility: Ethanol is highly mobile in soil and water (Koc: ~1 L/kg; log Kow = -0.31). It is miscible with water and expected to leach readily into groundwater.
iarc_classification: Group 1 (Alcoholic beverages are Group 1; ethanol in alcoholic beverages is a known human carcinogen)
ntp_classification: Known to be a human carcinogen (ethanol in alcoholic beverages)

regulatory.prop_65_warning: Ethanol (in alcoholic beverages) is listed under California Proposition 65 as a chemical known to cause cancer and developmental toxicity (reproductive toxicity - developmental).

name: Sodium Silicate 40%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.

persistence: Sodium silicate is an inorganic substance; biodegradation is not applicable. It hydrolyzes in water to form silicic acid and sodium hydroxide. It is not expected to persist as a discrete organic molecule.
bioaccumulation: The substance is inorganic and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: Sodium silicate is highly soluble in water and expected to be mobile in aquatic environments; it dissociates to silicate and sodium ions.

name: Sulfamic Acid

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause burns on prolonged or repeated contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause irritation to the respiratory tract upon inhalation of dust.

persistence: Sulfamic acid is expected to be readily biodegradable. It undergoes hydrolysis in water to form ammonium sulfate. It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow and high water solubility.
mobility: Sulfamic acid is highly water soluble and is expected to be highly mobile in soil and aquatic environments.

name: Dichloroisocyanuric Acid Sodium Salt Dihydrate (NaDCC)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause mild to moderate skin burns upon prolonged contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation via chlorine gas release.

persistence: The substance hydrolyzes rapidly in water releasing hypochlorous acid and cyanuric acid. Cyanuric acid is not readily biodegradable but degrades slowly under environmental conditions. The active chlorine moiety is not persistent. Overall persistence is low to moderate.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to rapid hydrolysis and low log Kow of degradation products. BCF is estimated to be low.
mobility: The substance and its hydrolysis products are highly mobile in aquatic environments. Cyanuric acid is water soluble and mobile in soil.

name: Salt Kiln Dried Medium Grade

toxicology.skin_result: Not expected to cause skin irritation under normal conditions of use.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause mild eye irritation. Dust may cause mechanical irritation.

persistence: Sodium chloride is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It is persistent in the environment as an ionic compound.
bioaccumulation: Sodium chloride is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its ionic nature and rapid excretion in organisms.
mobility: Sodium chloride is highly water soluble (360 g/L at 20°C) and highly mobile in aquatic and soil environments.

name: Calcium Hydroxide Powder

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation following repeated or prolonged inhalation exposure.

persistence: Calcium hydroxide is an inorganic substance; biodegradability is not applicable. It dissolves in water to form calcium ions and hydroxide ions, which are naturally occurring. The substance is not expected to persist as such in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is an inorganic salt and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms. Bioconcentration is not applicable for inorganic substances.
mobility: Calcium hydroxide dissociates in water into calcium and hydroxide ions. It is highly mobile in aquatic environments. Koc is not applicable for inorganic substances.

name: Sodium Percarbonate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause burns upon prolonged contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation of dust.

persistence: Sodium percarbonate rapidly decomposes in water to sodium carbonate and hydrogen peroxide. Hydrogen peroxide is readily degradable abiotically and biotically; the substance is not considered persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to rapid decomposition to inorganic products (sodium carbonate, hydrogen peroxide, water, oxygen). BCF is not applicable.
mobility: Sodium percarbonate decomposes rapidly in aqueous environments to sodium carbonate and hydrogen peroxide. The resulting ionic species are highly mobile in soil and water.

name: Methanol Tech Grade

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation with prolonged or repeated contact. Not classified as a skin corrosive.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes eye irritation. Vapors may cause watering and irritation of the eyes.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (optic nerve, central nervous system) through prolonged or repeated exposure. Classified STOT RE Category 1.

persistence: Methanol is readily biodegradable in water and soil. BOD5/ThOD ratio indicates rapid aerobic biodegradation. Atmospheric half-life is approximately 7-18 days via reaction with hydroxyl radicals.
bioaccumulation: Methanol is not expected to bioaccumulate in aquatic organisms. Log Kow = -0.77; estimated BCF < 1.
mobility: Methanol is highly mobile in soil and is miscible with water. Koc is estimated at approximately 1 L/kg; leaching to groundwater is likely.
iarc_classification: Not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans (Group 3) — Note: IARC has not formally assigned methanol to a group; no sufficient evidence for carcinogenicity.
ntp_classification: Not listed as a known or reasonably anticipated human carcinogen.

name: Sodium Sulfate

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.

persistence: Sodium sulfate is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It is persistent in the environment but not considered environmentally hazardous at typical concentrations.
bioaccumulation: Sodium sulfate is an inorganic ionic compound and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: Sodium sulfate is highly soluble in water and highly mobile in the environment. It readily dissociates into sodium and sulfate ions in aqueous solution.

name: D-Limonene

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. May cause skin sensitization.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation (STOT SE Category 3).

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. D-Limonene degrades rapidly under aerobic conditions in water and soil. Estimated half-life in air is short due to reaction with hydroxyl radicals.
bioaccumulation: The substance has low to moderate bioaccumulation potential [log Kow: 4.57; estimated BCF: ~260 L/kg].
mobility: The substance has low mobility in soil due to moderate lipophilicity (estimated Koc: ~1000 L/kg). It may adsorb to soil and sediment.

name: Tetrapotassium Pyrophosphate (TKPP)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: Tetrapotassium pyrophosphate hydrolyzes in water to orthophosphate ions and is not expected to persist. It is not considered a persistent organic substance.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. As an inorganic salt it dissociates in water; bioaccumulation is not relevant.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in aquatic environments due to its high water solubility and ionic nature. Adsorption to soil is low.

name: Decyl Amine Oxide

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is considered readily biodegradable based on its amine oxide structure and available biodegradation data.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to its ionic/zwitterionic nature at environmental pH (log Kow estimated < 1).
mobility: The substance is expected to be mobile in the aquatic environment; adsorption to soil or sediment is limited due to its surfactant character.

name: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate 30% (SLS)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: Sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) is readily biodegradable. It undergoes rapid aerobic biodegradation in water and soil. It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (~1.6) and ionic character. BCF is considered low.
mobility: The substance is expected to be highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low adsorption to soil particles (low Koc).

name: Sodium Metabisulfite

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. May cause burns on prolonged contact due to SO2 release.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation via SO2 liberation. Sensitizer in asthmatics.

persistence: Sodium metabisulfite is readily oxidized in water to sulfate, which is a naturally occurring anion. It is not considered persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its ionic nature and rapid conversion to inorganic sulfate.
mobility: The substance dissociates in water to sodium and metabisulfite/sulfite ions and is highly mobile in aquatic environments.

name: Trisodium Phosphate Anhydrous (TSP)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion due to strongly alkaline pH.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage (irreversible effects) due to strongly alkaline pH.

persistence: Inorganic phosphate salts are not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense. Phosphate is a naturally occurring inorganic nutrient; it does not biodegrade but is assimilated by biological systems and may contribute to eutrophication in aquatic environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic salt and does not have a meaningful log Kow or BCF.
mobility: Trisodium phosphate is highly soluble in water and dissociates completely to sodium and phosphate ions. Phosphate can adsorb to soils, particularly iron- and aluminum-rich soils, but the ionic species are mobile in aquatic environments.

name: Sodium Nitrite

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation upon prolonged or repeated contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause methemoglobinemia following significant systemic absorption; target organs include blood and cardiovascular system.

persistence: Sodium nitrite is not expected to be persistent in the environment. It is readily oxidized to nitrate in aerobic conditions and can be reduced under anaerobic conditions. It is not considered readily biodegradable in standard tests but undergoes rapid abiotic transformation in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Sodium nitrite is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its ionic nature and high water solubility. BCF is not applicable for inorganic salts.
mobility: Sodium nitrite is highly mobile in soil and water environments due to its high water solubility and ionic character. It does not adsorb significantly to soil particles.
iarc_classification: Group 2A (Ingested nitrites under conditions that result in endogenous nitrosation)

regulatory.prop_65_warning: Sodium nitrite is listed under California Proposition 65 as a chemical known to the State of California to cause cancer.

name: Sodium Metasilicate Pentahydrate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.

persistence: Sodium metasilicate pentahydrate is an inorganic substance; biodegradation is not applicable. It dissociates in water to sodium ions and silicate ions. Silicate is a naturally occurring inorganic ion and is not considered persistent in the conventional sense.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic salt that dissociates in water; log Kow and BCF are not applicable.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in water. It readily dissolves and dissociates into sodium and silicate ions. Adsorption to soil is expected to be moderate to low.

name: Soda Ash Dense (Sodium Carbonate)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; prolonged contact may cause burns.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation following inhalation of dust.

persistence: Sodium carbonate is an inorganic substance and the concept of biodegradability does not apply. It dissociates in water to sodium and carbonate ions, which are naturally occurring. It is not persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic salt that dissociates in aqueous solution; bioaccumulation potential is negligible.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in aqueous environments. It is highly soluble in water (215 g/L at 20°C) and dissociates into ions. Koc is not applicable for inorganic salts.

name: CMC (Carboxymethyl Cellulose)

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant.

persistence: Carboxymethyl cellulose is a cellulose derivative and is considered biodegradable under aerobic conditions, though it is not classified as readily biodegradable in standard OECD tests. It is expected to undergo slow environmental degradation.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its high molecular weight and hydrophilic polymer nature.
mobility: Due to its polymeric nature and high molecular weight, CMC has low mobility in soil and is expected to adsorb to sediment and soil particles.

name: Alkyldimethylbenzylammonium Chloride (ADBAC)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. However, it may be persistent under anaerobic conditions due to adsorption to sediment and sludge. Biodegradation in water is rapid once adapted microbial communities are present.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to its ionic nature and high water solubility. Log Kow is low for the ionised form.
mobility: The substance has low mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to organic matter and clay minerals (high Koc). It is unlikely to leach into groundwater.

name: NTA Powder (Nitrilotriacetic Acid)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation of dust.

persistence: Nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA) is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. It is rapidly mineralized by microorganisms in activated sludge and surface waters. Under anaerobic conditions biodegradation is slower. Half-life in surface water is estimated at a few days to weeks under favorable conditions.
bioaccumulation: NTA is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow (log Kow ≈ -3.5) and high water solubility. BCF is estimated to be very low (<10).
mobility: NTA is highly mobile in the environment due to its high water solubility and low soil adsorption coefficient (Koc estimated at approximately 10–100 L/kg). It is expected to leach into groundwater.
ntp_classification: Reasonably Anticipated to be a Human Carcinogen

regulatory.prop_65_warning: Nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA) is listed on the California Proposition 65 list as a substance known to the State of California to cause cancer.

name: Oleic Acid

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.

persistence: Oleic acid is readily biodegradable (>60% degradation in 28 days under OECD 301 conditions). It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Oleic acid is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to rapid metabolism. Log Kow approximately 7.64, but BCF is estimated to be low due to biotransformation.
mobility: Oleic acid has low mobility in soil due to its high log Kow and tendency to adsorb to organic matter (estimated Koc: ~100000 L/kg).

name: Caprylic Acid

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: Caprylic acid is readily biodegradable. It is expected to biodegrade rapidly in the environment based on its natural occurrence as a fatty acid.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly (log Kow: 3.05; BCF estimated low).
mobility: The substance has moderate mobility in soil (log Koc estimated ~2.1). It may adsorb to soil and sediment to some degree.

name: ATMP 50%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is not readily biodegradable. ATMP is persistent in the aquatic environment and resistant to biological degradation under standard test conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (log Kow < -2) and high water solubility.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc; however, it may adsorb to soil particles and sediments via complexation with metal ions.

name: Gluconic Acid 50%

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant at low concentrations; concentrated solutions may cause mild irritation.

persistence: Gluconic acid is readily biodegradable and not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Gluconic acid is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow (log Kow: -1.84).
mobility: Gluconic acid is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc.

name: Sodium Lignosulfonate

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant at concentrations tested.

persistence: Sodium lignosulfonate is a complex polymeric substance derived from lignin. It is not readily biodegradable under standard test conditions (e.g., OECD 301), though it may undergo slow biological transformation. It is considered persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: Due to its high molecular weight and polymeric nature, sodium lignosulfonate is not expected to bioaccumulate in aquatic organisms.
mobility: Sodium lignosulfonate is highly water soluble and may be mobile in soil and aquatic environments; however, it can adsorb to soil particles due to its polymeric structure.

name: Cyclohexylamine TG

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. BOD/COD ratio indicates rapid mineralization under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly (log Kow: 1.49; estimated BCF low).
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its low Koc and high water solubility.

name: Lactic Acid 88%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; concentrated solutions may cause burns.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye irritation; concentrated solutions may cause serious eye damage.

persistence: L-Lactic acid (CAS 79-33-4) is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions and is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (log Kow = -0.62) and high water solubility.
mobility: The substance is expected to be highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low adsorption to soil particles (estimated Koc: ~1 L/kg).

name: p-Toluenesulfonic Acid (From Pyxis)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.

persistence: p-Toluenesulfonic acid is considered readily biodegradable based on its structural properties and available data.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (estimated < 1).
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low adsorption potential.

name: LEVASIL (Colloidal Silica)

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions (amorphous colloidal silica suspension).
toxicology.stot_result: Repeated inhalation exposure to amorphous silica dust may cause effects on the respiratory system.

persistence: Amorphous silica (colloidal) is an inorganic substance; biodegradability is not applicable. It is considered persistent in the environment but is a naturally occurring mineral substance.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Amorphous silica is an inorganic material with no meaningful log Kow or BCF.
mobility: Colloidal silica particles may remain suspended in water and can be mobile in aquatic environments; mobility in soil is limited due to adsorption.

name: Acetonitrile (OPTIMA)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness. Causes damage to organs (central nervous system, liver, kidneys) through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: Acetonitrile is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. It is not expected to persist in the environment. Atmospheric half-life is approximately 363 days (reaction with OH radicals).
bioaccumulation: Acetonitrile is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly (log Kow: -0.34; estimated BCF: 3.2).
mobility: Acetonitrile is highly mobile in soil and is expected to leach into groundwater (Koc: approximately 24 L/kg). It is miscible with water.

name: Sodium Thiocyanate

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause effects on the thyroid gland with repeated or prolonged exposure.

persistence: Sodium thiocyanate is expected to be biodegradable under aerobic conditions; thiocyanate can be degraded by microorganisms in soil and water, though it may persist in anaerobic environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to its ionic nature and low log Kow.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its ionic character and high water solubility.

name: CALCHEM D5 (Decamethylcyclopentasiloxane)

toxicology.skin_result: Not irritating to skin.
toxicology.stot_result: Repeated inhalation exposure may cause effects on the liver and uterus in rats.

persistence: Decamethylcyclopentasiloxane (D5) is not readily biodegradable in water; it is persistent in aquatic environments. It undergoes atmospheric degradation with an estimated half-life of approximately 10 days via OH radical reaction.
bioaccumulation: D5 has potential for bioaccumulation based on its high log Kow (8.03). BCF values measured in fish range up to approximately 5900 (wet weight), though some studies suggest metabolism reduces actual bioaccumulation.
mobility: D5 has low water solubility (~0.017 mg/L at 25°C) and high Koc (~4100 L/kg), indicating low mobility in soil and strong adsorption to sediment and organic matter.

name: CALCHEM TBP (Tributyl Phosphate)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation with prolonged or repeated contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (nervous system) through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: Tributyl phosphate is not readily biodegradable based on standard tests; however, it may be degraded under certain environmental conditions. It has a half-life in water estimated at several weeks to months.
bioaccumulation: The substance has low potential to bioaccumulate (log Kow = 4.0; BCF estimated ~119 L/kg).
mobility: Moderately mobile in soil (Koc estimated ~900 L/kg); has some potential to leach into groundwater.

name: DEAE (Diethylethanolamine)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin burns and corrosion.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable based on OECD 301 test data. Biodegradation in water is expected to be rapid under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (log Kow: -0.58). BCF is estimated to be low.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low estimated Koc value.

name: Sodium Borate (Borax)

toxicology.skin_result: Mild skin irritant; not classified as causing severe burns.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation upon inhalation of dust.

persistence: Boron is an inorganic element and does not biodegrade in the conventional sense. It persists in aquatic and soil environments as borate ion. Not readily biodegradable (concept of biodegradation is not applicable to inorganic substances).
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly; log Kow is not applicable for inorganic borates. BCF is low.
mobility: Highly mobile in soil and water due to high water solubility (~31 g/L at 20°C). Borate ions do not bind strongly to soil particles (low Koc).

regulatory.prop_65_warning: Sodium borate (borax) is listed on the California Proposition 65 list as a developmental/reproductive toxicant (developmental toxicity, male reproductive toxicity).

name: Cobaltous Sulfate Heptahydrate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. May cause sensitization by skin contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (lungs, heart) through prolonged or repeated exposure. Suspected of causing genetic defects. May cause cancer via inhalation.

persistence: Cobalt sulfate heptahydrate is an inorganic substance and is not subject to biodegradation. Cobalt ions persist in the aquatic environment and do not degrade. The substance is considered persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance has low potential for bioaccumulation. Cobalt is an essential trace element but at elevated concentrations may accumulate in aquatic organisms to a limited extent (BCF: approximately 40 L/kg for aquatic organisms).
mobility: Cobalt sulfate is highly soluble in water (approximately 603 g/L at 20°C). Cobalt ions are highly mobile in aquatic environments. In soil, cobalt may bind to organic matter and clay minerals, reducing mobility (Koc variable, typically 100–1000 L/kg depending on soil type and pH).
iarc_classification: Group 2B — Cobalt sulfate is possibly carcinogenic to humans (IARC Monograph Vol. 86, 2006).
ntp_classification: Reasonably anticipated to be a human carcinogen (NTP 15th Report on Carcinogens: Cobalt and cobalt compounds that release cobalt ions in vivo).

regulatory.prop_65_warning: WARNING: Cobaltous sulfate heptahydrate (cobalt and cobalt compounds) is known to the State of California to cause cancer.

name: Potassium Bicarbonate

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under normal conditions.

persistence: Potassium bicarbonate is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It dissociates in water to potassium and bicarbonate ions, which are naturally occurring constituents of the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic ionic compound with no tendency for bioconcentration.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in aqueous environments as it fully dissociates into potassium and bicarbonate ions upon dissolution.

name: Propylene Glycol 99.9% Tech

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under normal conditions.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable in water. BOD5/COD ratio indicates rapid aerobic biodegradation. Not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Log Kow = -0.92; BCF is estimated to be very low.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil (Koc: approximately 1 L/kg). High water solubility (miscible) suggests potential for leaching into groundwater.

name: Tartaric Acid

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation upon prolonged contact.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause mild to moderate eye irritation.

persistence: Tartaric acid is readily biodegradable and is expected to be rapidly mineralized in both aerobic and anaerobic environments.
bioaccumulation: Tartaric acid is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its high water solubility and low log Kow (estimated log Kow: -1.00).
mobility: Tartaric acid is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc.

name: Morpholine

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation with repeated exposure.

persistence: Morpholine is readily biodegradable. BOD5/COD ratio and aerobic biodegradation tests indicate rapid biodegradation in the environment. Half-life in water is expected to be short.
bioaccumulation: Morpholine is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow (-1.08). BCF is estimated to be very low (< 10).
mobility: Morpholine is highly mobile in soil (log Koc approximately 0.6–1.0). It is highly soluble in water (miscible) and expected to leach readily into groundwater.

name: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)

toxicology.skin_result: Not classified as a skin irritant based on available data.
toxicology.eye_result: Not classified as an eye irritant based on available data.

persistence: No reliable data available on biodegradability for DHEA (CAS 53-43-0). The substance is not readily classified based on current available information.
bioaccumulation: No reliable BCF data available for DHEA. Based on estimated log Kow (~3.3), moderate bioaccumulation potential cannot be excluded.
mobility: Moderate mobility expected based on physicochemical properties. Exact Koc not established.

name: Hydrofluoric Acid 49%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns; penetrates skin rapidly causing deep tissue destruction and systemic fluoride toxicity.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; contact may result in severe burns and permanent injury.
toxicology.stot_result: Target organs: bones, teeth, kidneys, heart. Repeated or prolonged exposure may cause fluorosis of teeth and skeleton.

persistence: Hydrogen fluoride dissociates in water to fluoride ions. Fluoride is a naturally occurring inorganic ion; it is not biodegradable. In the environment, fluoride persists and may precipitate as insoluble calcium fluoride depending on calcium availability.
bioaccumulation: Fluoride is an inorganic ion and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms via lipophilic mechanisms. BCF is not applicable for inorganic ions.
mobility: Hydrogen fluoride is highly soluble in water and dissociates to fluoride ion, which is highly mobile in aqueous environments. Adsorption to soil depends on soil pH and mineral content; fluoride may leach to groundwater under certain conditions.

name: DTPMPA

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is not readily biodegradable based on available data. DTPMPA is a phosphonate chelating agent that is resistant to biological degradation under standard test conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow and high water solubility.
mobility: The substance is expected to be mobile in aquatic environments. It may adsorb to soils and sediments due to its phosphonate groups.

name: Sodium Chlorite 31%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue damage. Corrosive to skin.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage. Corrosive to eyes.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation and damage following inhalation of vapors or mists. Target organs: respiratory tract, blood.

persistence: Sodium chlorite is an inorganic oxidizing salt that undergoes chemical reduction to chloride in aquatic and soil environments. It is not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense; it is expected to be converted to chloride ion in the environment and is not considered persistent as the parent compound.
bioaccumulation: Sodium chlorite is an inorganic ionic compound and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: As an ionic inorganic salt, sodium chlorite is highly mobile in aquatic and soil environments and is not expected to adsorb significantly to soil particles.

name: Phenoxyethanol (Cola-Fax 3383)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness at high concentrations.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. Phenoxyethanol has been shown to biodegrade rapidly in standard biodegradability tests (>60% within 28 days).
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Log Kow = 1.16; BCF estimated to be low.
mobility: The substance is expected to be highly mobile in soil (log Koc estimated ~1.7). Leaching into groundwater is possible.

name: Aluminum Sulfate Dry Iron Free

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild to moderate skin irritation upon prolonged or repeated contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye irritation; may cause eye damage upon direct contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation of dust.

persistence: Aluminum sulfate is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It dissociates in water to aluminum and sulfate ions. Persistence as an organic compound is not applicable; the ionic species are persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Aluminum sulfate is an inorganic salt and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms. Bioconcentration factor (BCF) data are not applicable for inorganic salts.
mobility: Aluminum sulfate dissociates in water to aluminum and sulfate ions. Aluminum ions may adsorb to soil particles and sediment depending on pH; mobility is pH-dependent. Sulfate ions are highly mobile in soil and water.

name: Calcium Chloride FG

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: Calcium chloride is an inorganic salt; biodegradation is not applicable. It does not degrade in the environment but dissociates into calcium and chloride ions in water.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic salt that ionizes completely in aqueous solution; BCF is not relevant.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil and water due to its high water solubility (~745 g/L at 20°C). It readily dissociates into ions.

name: Propionic Acid

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue damage on prolonged contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; risk of permanent injury.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause irritation to the respiratory tract on repeated or prolonged exposure.

persistence: Propionic acid is readily biodegradable. It degrades rapidly under aerobic conditions and is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate (log Kow: 0.33; BCF estimated < 10).
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its low Koc (estimated Koc: ~1 L/kg) and high water solubility.

name: Sodium Bicarbonate

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard GHS classification.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause mild eye irritation; not classified as serious eye damage.

persistence: Sodium bicarbonate is an inorganic salt and not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense. It dissociates in water to sodium and bicarbonate ions, which are naturally occurring constituents of the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. As an inorganic salt, bioaccumulation potential is not applicable.
mobility: Sodium bicarbonate is highly water-soluble and highly mobile in aquatic environments. It dissociates completely in water.

name: Potassium Permanganate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and tissue damage; strong oxidizer causing chemical burns on contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; corrosive to eye tissue.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation of dust or aerosol.

persistence: Potassium permanganate is an inorganic oxidizing agent. It is not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense; it decomposes in water to form manganese dioxide and other manganese species. The concept of biodegradability is not applicable to inorganic substances.
bioaccumulation: Bioaccumulation is not expected. Potassium permanganate is an inorganic salt; as an oxidizing agent it reacts rapidly in biological and aquatic systems, yielding manganese dioxide. Bioconcentration is not considered relevant.
mobility: Potassium permanganate is highly soluble in water (65 g/L at 20°C) and is highly mobile in aquatic and soil environments. It is rapidly reduced in contact with organic matter or reducing agents.

name: Calcium Hypochlorite

toxicology.skin_result: Causes severe skin burns and skin corrosion.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause irritation of the respiratory tract; repeated or prolonged exposure may cause damage to organs (respiratory system).

persistence: Calcium hypochlorite rapidly dissociates in water to release hypochlorite ions (OCl-), which are further broken down by light, temperature, and reaction with organic matter. The substance is not considered persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its ionic nature and rapid degradation in aquatic environments.
mobility: Calcium hypochlorite is highly soluble in water and is expected to be highly mobile in the aquatic environment. It rapidly dissociates upon contact with water.

name: Iodine

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation and burns; repeated or prolonged contact may cause sensitization.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye irritation and potential damage.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation; thyroid effects reported with chronic exposure.

persistence: Iodine is an inorganic elemental substance and is not subject to biodegradation. It reacts with water to form iodide and iodate species; environmental persistence depends on speciation, pH, and redox conditions. Not readily biodegradable in the conventional sense.
bioaccumulation: Iodine (as iodide) may be taken up by marine organisms, particularly algae, but the bioconcentration potential of elemental iodine per se is not considered significant in standard assessments. BCF data for elemental iodine are not well established.
mobility: Iodine is slightly soluble in water; in the environment it rapidly converts to iodide, which is highly mobile in soil and water (Koc low). Elemental iodine itself has limited mobility due to reactions with organic matter and reduction to iodide.

name: DL-Malic Acid

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: DL-Malic acid is readily biodegradable and is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (log Kow: -1.26).
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc.

name: Allantoin

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.
toxicology.eye_result: Not a serious eye irritant under standard test conditions.

persistence: Allantoin is expected to be readily biodegradable based on its structure as a naturally occurring purine metabolite. No significant persistence in the environment is anticipated.
bioaccumulation: Allantoin is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow (estimated log Kow < 0) and high water solubility.
mobility: Allantoin is highly water soluble and is expected to be highly mobile in soil and aquatic environments.

name: Sorbitol

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.
toxicology.eye_result: Not a serious eye irritant under standard test conditions.

persistence: Sorbitol is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Sorbitol is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (approximately -2.2) and high water solubility.
mobility: Sorbitol is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low Koc. It is expected to leach into groundwater.

name: Cobalt Nitrate Hexahydrate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. May cause sensitization by skin contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (lungs, heart) through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate is an inorganic salt; the concept of biodegradability does not apply. The cobalt ion persists in the environment and is not degraded. The nitrate ion is subject to biological transformation (denitrification) in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly. Cobalt has a low bioconcentration potential (BCF < 100).
mobility: The substance is highly soluble in water and highly mobile in the aquatic environment. Cobalt ions may adsorb to soil particles depending on pH and organic content (Koc variable).
iarc_classification: Group 2A (cobalt and cobalt compounds, inhalation exposure in hard-metal and cobalt dust industries; cobalt metal with tungsten carbide). Cobalt(II) compounds overall: Group 2B.
ntp_classification: Reasonably Anticipated to be a Human Carcinogen (cobalt and cobalt compounds).

regulatory.prop_65_warning: WARNING: This product contains cobalt and cobalt compounds, known to the State of California to cause cancer.

name: Diethylhydroxylamine (DEHA)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation following inhalation exposure.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable based on available data. Diethylhydroxylamine is expected to degrade relatively quickly in the aquatic environment under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly. Estimated log Kow is approximately 0.21, indicating low bioaccumulation potential.
mobility: The substance is highly mobile in soil due to its low log Kow and high water solubility.

name: Sodium Persulfate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause skin sensitization.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation and sensitization upon repeated or prolonged inhalation exposure.

persistence: Sodium persulfate is an inorganic oxidizing salt that hydrolyzes rapidly in water to form sulfate ions. It is not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense; it decomposes abiotically. The substance is not considered persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is an inorganic salt and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: As an inorganic salt with high water solubility, sodium persulfate is highly mobile in aquatic and soil environments.

name: Potassium Metabisulfite (KMBS)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause burns on prolonged contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye irritation; may cause eye damage.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause irritation of the respiratory tract upon inhalation of dust or generated sulfur dioxide.

persistence: Potassium metabisulfite is readily oxidized in aqueous solution to sulfate, which is the stable end product. The substance is not considered persistent in the environment due to rapid chemical transformation. It is not readily biodegradable in the conventional sense but undergoes rapid abiotic degradation.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its ionic nature and rapid conversion to sulfate in aqueous media. LogPow is not applicable for this inorganic salt.
mobility: As an inorganic salt, potassium metabisulfite is highly soluble in water and highly mobile in the environment. Adsorption to soil is expected to be low.

name: Calcium Acetate

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation upon prolonged contact.

persistence: Calcium acetate is readily biodegradable. The acetate anion is rapidly metabolized by microorganisms under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow and ionic character.
mobility: Calcium acetate is highly water soluble and is expected to be highly mobile in the environment.

name: Potassium Carbonate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation and may cause burns with prolonged contact.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage (corrosive to eyes).

persistence: Potassium carbonate is an inorganic salt that dissociates in water to potassium and carbonate ions. It is not subject to biodegradation. Carbonate equilibria are governed by natural buffering systems; the substance is not persistent in the environmental sense applicable to organic compounds.
bioaccumulation: Potassium carbonate is an inorganic electrolyte that dissociates completely in water. Bioaccumulation is not expected; BCF is not applicable for inorganic salts.
mobility: Potassium carbonate is highly soluble in water (1120 g/L at 20°C) and dissociates to K+ and CO3(2-) ions; it is expected to be highly mobile in aquatic environments. Koc is not applicable for this inorganic salt.

name: Sodium Bisulfite

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause burns with prolonged contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause irritation to the respiratory tract upon inhalation of dust or aerosol.

persistence: Sodium bisulfite is readily oxidized to sulfate in the environment and is not persistent. It is considered readily biodegradable/abiotically degradable in water.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic salt with negligible log Kow.
mobility: Sodium bisulfite is highly water soluble and highly mobile in aquatic environments. It readily dissociates into sodium and bisulfite ions.

name: Copper Sulfate Crystals

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; prolonged contact may cause burns.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (liver, kidneys) through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: Copper sulfate is an inorganic salt; it does not biodegrade in the conventional sense. Copper ion persists in the environment and is not subject to biodegradation. It may adsorb to sediments and soil particles.
bioaccumulation: Copper has a low potential to bioaccumulate in organisms. BCF values for copper in fish are generally low (BCF: 9–196 L/kg depending on species and conditions). Essential element at low concentrations; regulated at higher concentrations.
mobility: Copper ions in soil have moderate to low mobility due to strong adsorption to soil organic matter and clay minerals (Koc approximately 100–1000 L/kg depending on soil type). In aqueous environments, mobility is pH-dependent.

name: EDTA Free Acid

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.

persistence: EDTA (free acid) is not readily biodegradable under standard test conditions. It is persistent in the aquatic environment and resistant to conventional aerobic biodegradation, though some biodegradation can occur under specific conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its low log Kow (approximately -3.86) and high water solubility.
mobility: EDTA is highly mobile in the environment due to its high water solubility and low soil adsorption coefficient (Koc: approximately 10 L/kg).

name: Calcium Nitrite

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause methemoglobinemia upon systemic absorption; may affect blood.

persistence: Calcium nitrite is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense. Nitrite ion may be oxidized to nitrate by nitrifying bacteria in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic ionic compound with negligible log Kow.
mobility: Highly mobile in aqueous environments due to its high water solubility. The nitrite ion is not expected to adsorb to soil or sediment.

name: RO Water

toxicology.skin_result: Not irritating.

persistence: Water is not a organic substance and is not subject to biodegradation assessments. It is an inorganic solvent and does not persist in the environment in any hazardous sense.
bioaccumulation: Water does not bioaccumulate. Not applicable.
mobility: Water is highly mobile in all environmental compartments.

name: Chrysoidine Y (Basic Orange 2)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause harm to organs through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: The substance is not readily biodegradable. Azo dyes such as Basic Orange 2 are generally persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to significantly bioaccumulate based on its ionic nature and low log Kow.
mobility: The substance is expected to be mobile in aquatic environments due to its water solubility; adsorption to soil is limited.

name: FD&C Blue 1 (Brilliant Blue FCF)

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.

persistence: Not readily biodegradable based on available data; the azo-related aromatic sulfonate structure is expected to be resistant to biodegradation under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its high molecular weight and ionic character (BCF estimated <100).
mobility: The substance is highly water-soluble and ionic; expected to be mobile in aquatic environments. Low adsorption to soil expected.

name: Rhodamine B 400%

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.

persistence: Rhodamine B is not readily biodegradable. It is resistant to aerobic biodegradation under standard test conditions and may persist in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance has low bioaccumulation potential based on its physicochemical properties (log Pow approximately 1.95).
mobility: The substance has moderate mobility in soil. It may adsorb to sediment and suspended particles due to its cationic nature.

name: Permalon Uranine (Fluorescein Sodium)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: No reliable data on ready biodegradability is available for fluorescein sodium. The substance is not expected to be readily biodegradable based on its aromatic structure.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly based on its low log Kow and high water solubility.
mobility: The substance is expected to be highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and ionic character.

name: FD&C Red Dye 40 (Allura Red)

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant based on available data.

persistence: Allura Red AC is an azo dye that is not readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. It may undergo reductive cleavage of the azo bond under anaerobic conditions, potentially generating aromatic amine metabolites.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to its high molecular weight and ionic character (sulfonate groups). Low log Kow.
mobility: The substance is expected to have low mobility in soil due to its ionic nature and tendency to adsorb to soil particles.

name: Tricoblanc CBS Powder (Optical Brightener)

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant based on available data.

persistence: The substance is not readily biodegradable based on available data.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly based on its physicochemical properties.
mobility: The substance has moderate mobility in soil based on its ionic nature and water solubility.

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.

name: Xanthan Gum Powder

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under normal conditions of use.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause mild mechanical irritation to eyes.
toxicology.stot_result: Inhalation of dust may cause respiratory irritation. No specific target organ toxicity identified at relevant doses.

persistence: Xanthan gum is a natural polysaccharide and is readily biodegradable under environmental conditions. It is not considered persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Xanthan gum is a high molecular weight polysaccharide and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms. Log Pow and BCF values are not applicable for this polymeric substance.
mobility: As a high molecular weight polymer, xanthan gum has low mobility in soil. It is expected to adsorb to soil particles and is unlikely to leach significantly into groundwater.

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation.

name: Potassium silicate, anhydrous

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; strongly alkaline solutions cause severe skin burns.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage; strongly alkaline, may cause irreversible eye damage.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation of dust.

persistence: Potassium silicate is an inorganic substance and is not subject to biodegradation.
