The silicate component hydrolyzes in water to form silicic acid, which is a naturally occurring substance. Persistence assessment by standard biodegradability tests is not applicable to inorganic substances.
bioaccumulation: Potassium silicate is an inorganic salt and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms. Bioconcentration factor (BCF) data are not applicable.
mobility: Potassium silicate dissolves readily in water to form silicate and potassium ions. Silicate ions may adsorb to soil minerals; mobility in soil is considered low to moderate depending on soil pH and composition. Koc data are not applicable for this inorganic substance.

name: HPMA (homopolymer of maleic acid) 50%

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation on prolonged or repeated contact.

persistence: The substance is a synthetic polymer and is not readily biodegradable. Hydrolysis and photodegradation in the aquatic environment are expected to be slow.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its polymeric nature and high water solubility. BCF is expected to be low.
mobility: The substance is highly water soluble and expected to be mobile in the aquatic environment. Adsorption to soil is expected to be low.

name: Rheocare HSP-1180

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant based on available data.
toxicology.eye_result: Not an eye irritant based on available data.

persistence: No data available on biodegradability for this polymeric modified starch. As a high molecular weight polysaccharide derivative, it is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Not expected to bioaccumulate due to high molecular weight polymeric nature.
mobility: Low mobility expected in soil due to high molecular weight polymeric structure.

name: Dodecylbenzene (DDBSA)

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation and corrosion; classified as a skin corrosive (Category 1).
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory tract irritation upon inhalation of mists or vapors.

persistence: Dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid (CAS 27176-87-0) is considered readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. Primary biodegradation is well documented for linear alkylbenzene sulfonates. Ultimate biodegradation occurs under aerobic conditions, though persistence in anaerobic sediment environments may be greater.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly based on its physicochemical properties and surfactant nature. Estimated BCF is low (BCF < 500).
mobility: The substance has moderate to low mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to sediment and organic matter (estimated Koc: 1000–10000 L/kg). Mobility in aquatic environments is affected by its surfactant properties.

name: Norfox 1101

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; known skin sensitizer.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. BOD/COD ratio indicates rapid aerobic biodegradation in aquatic environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to its zwitterionic nature and low log Kow.
mobility: The substance is expected to have moderate mobility in soil due to its amphoteric/surfactant character.

name: Tall Oil Fatty Acid

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: Tall oil fatty acids are readily biodegradable. The substance is expected to biodegrade rapidly in aquatic and terrestrial environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly based on its physical-chemical properties and ready biodegradability.
mobility: Low to moderate mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to organic matter. Koc estimated to be high given the long fatty acid chain lengths.

name: Silicone PDMS emulsion, 30%

toxicology.skin_result: Non-irritating to skin based on available data for PDMS emulsions.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause mild, transient eye irritation; not classified as serious eye damage.

persistence: PDMS (polydimethylsiloxane) polymer is not readily biodegradable in water. The high molecular weight polymer component is considered persistent in the aquatic environment. The aqueous emulsion carrier components may degrade more readily.
bioaccumulation: PDMS polymer is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its high molecular weight and low bioavailability. BCF is considered low for the polymeric siloxane component.
mobility: PDMS polymer has very low mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to organic matter and sediment (high Koc). The aqueous emulsion phase is mobile in water.

name: Mineral Spirit

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. Defatting of skin may occur on prolonged or repeated contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness. Repeated exposure may cause central nervous system depression. May cause damage to organs (central nervous system, kidneys) through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: Not readily biodegradable based on standard OECD tests. The substance contains aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons which are inherently biodegradable but may persist in the environment under anaerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance has moderate potential to bioaccumulate based on log Kow values of constituent hydrocarbons (estimated log Kow 3–7). BCF values for individual components are generally below 2000.
mobility: Low to moderate mobility in soil. The substance has a high affinity for organic matter (estimated Koc: 400–10000 L/kg depending on fraction). Volatilisation from water surface is expected.

name: MAQUAT MQ 2525M 50%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause burns at higher concentrations.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation.

persistence: Quaternary ammonium compounds of this type are considered readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions; however, they may be persistent in anaerobic environments and can adsorb strongly to sediments and sludge, reducing bioavailability.
bioaccumulation: Not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to high water solubility and ionic nature; however, BCF data are limited for this compound class.
mobility: Low mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to organic matter and clay particles (high Koc). The substance binds strongly to sediment and suspended matter.

name: ACCOSOFT 501 DR400

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is considered inherently biodegradable. Quaternary ammonium compounds of this class are known to adsorb to sediments and sludge, which may slow environmental degradation.
bioaccumulation: The substance has moderate potential for bioaccumulation due to its lipophilic nature; however, sorption to particulate matter limits bioavailability.
mobility: The substance has low mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to organic matter and negatively charged surfaces (high Koc expected).

name: Sodium Alkylbenzene Sulfonate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. Linear alkylbenzene sulfonates (LAS) are rapidly biodegraded under aerobic conditions in the environment, with >90% primary biodegradation typically observed.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly in aquatic organisms due to its ionic nature and low log Kow.
mobility: The substance is considered mobile in the aquatic environment. It adsorbs to sediment and sludge due to its surfactant nature, with moderate sorption to soil particles.

name: GBS Q-24

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation; may cause sensitization.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause respiratory irritation upon inhalation.

persistence: The substance is not readily biodegradable under standard OECD test conditions; however, it may biodegrade under adapted conditions. It is persistent in the aquatic environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance has low bioaccumulation potential based on its physicochemical properties; log Kow is not reliably determinable due to surfactant nature.
mobility: The substance is expected to have low mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to organic matter and sediment (high Koc).

name: C10 Linear Alcohol Ethoxylate/SURFONIC LF-17

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable based on standard OECD screening tests for alcohol ethoxylate surfactants of this carbon chain length and ethoxylation degree.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to significantly bioaccumulate due to its hydrophilic ethoxylate moiety; log Kow and BCF values are low for this class of surfactant.
mobility: The substance has moderate to high mobility in the aquatic environment; it is water-soluble and surfactant properties facilitate distribution. Adsorption to soil/sediment is possible (Koc estimated moderate for this class).

name: C12 Linear Alcohol Ethoxylate

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild to moderate skin irritation.
toxicology.eye_result: Causes serious eye damage (irritation to eyes).

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. Biodegradation in water has been shown to exceed 60% within 28 days under OECD 301 test conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly based on its physical-chemical properties and rapid biodegradation.
mobility: The substance has moderate mobility in soil. It is expected to partition primarily to water due to its surfactant nature.

name: AOS 40

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable. Alpha-olefin sulfonates are reported to biodegrade rapidly under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to its ionic/surfactant nature and low log Kow.
mobility: The substance is expected to have moderate to high mobility in soil given its surfactant properties and water solubility.

name: Polyethylene glycol oleamide (PEG-6)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: No reliable data available on biodegradability for this specific substance. As a polyethylene glycol-based fatty acid amide, it is expected to be inherently biodegradable based on structural analogy, but ready biodegradability has not been confirmed.
bioaccumulation: Not expected to bioaccumulate based on high molecular weight and hydrophilic polyethylene glycol chain. Specific BCF data not available.
mobility: Mobility in soil is expected to be moderate given the amphiphilic nature of the molecule. Specific Koc data not available.

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild to moderate skin irritation.

name: Isopropylamine Dodecylbenzene Sulfonate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is expected to be readily biodegradable based on its surfactant structure (linear alkylbenzene sulfonate backbone). It undergoes aerobic biodegradation in aquatic environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly based on its ionic surfactant nature and high water solubility.
mobility: The substance is moderately mobile in soil. As an anionic surfactant salt, it may adsorb to soil particles but retains some mobility in aquatic environments.

name: Cocoamide DEA

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable based on structural analogy with related fatty acid amides; expected to biodegrade rapidly in aquatic environments.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate significantly due to its amphiphilic nature and ready biodegradability.
mobility: The substance has low to moderate mobility in soil due to its amphiphilic character and tendency to adsorb onto soil organic matter.
iarc_classification: Group 2B (Coconut oil diethanolamine condensate listed as possibly carcinogenic to humans by IARC Monograph Vol. 101)

regulatory.prop_65_warning: Cocamide diethanolamine (Cocamide DEA) is known to the State of California to cause cancer.

name: Colateric 2CM

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild to moderate skin irritation upon prolonged or repeated contact.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable based on data for fatty alcohol ethoxylates in the C12-16 range.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to significantly bioaccumulate based on its physicochemical properties.

name: SLES 70%

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation.

persistence: The substance is readily biodegradable based on OECD 301 test methods. It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. Log Kow is low and BCF is estimated to be low.
mobility: The substance is expected to be mobile in soil given its high water solubility.

name: PE 600 Deceth 4 Phosphate

toxicology.skin_result: May cause skin irritation or burns (phosphate ester; corrosive potential).
toxicology.eye_result: May cause serious eye irritation or damage (phosphate ester; corrosive potential).

persistence: Ethoxylated phosphate ester surfactants are not readily biodegradable under standard OECD test conditions.
bioaccumulation: Not expected to bioaccumulate due to high hydrophilicity of ethoxylated phosphate esters.
mobility: Highly mobile in aquatic environments due to water solubility of ethoxylated phosphate esters.

name: Pine Oil 85% Tech Grade

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. May cause mild to moderate irritation on prolonged or repeated contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness upon inhalation of vapors. Aspiration hazard if swallowed.

persistence: Pine oil is expected to be readily biodegradable based on its terpene hydrocarbon composition. Rapid biological degradation is anticipated under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: Pine oil has moderate log Kow values for its major components (alpha-terpineol log Kow ~2.98); bioaccumulation potential is considered low to moderate.
mobility: Pine oil components have moderate mobility in soil. The substance may leach to groundwater to a limited extent. Koc values for major terpene alcohols are moderate.

name: Mineral Oil

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.
toxicology.eye_result: Not classified as an eye irritant.
toxicology.stot_result: Repeated or prolonged inhalation of mist may cause respiratory tract irritation and potential lung effects (lipoid pneumonia).

persistence: Mineral oil (CAS 8042-47-5) is not readily biodegradable based on standard OECD test criteria. It is expected to persist in the environment, particularly in soil and sediment, due to its complex hydrocarbon composition.
bioaccumulation: The substance has low to moderate bioaccumulation potential. Log Kow values for individual hydrocarbon components vary widely; as a complex mixture, significant bioaccumulation is not expected for the bulk substance.
mobility: Low mobility in soil due to strong adsorption to organic matter (high Koc). The substance is not expected to leach significantly into groundwater.
iarc_classification: Group 1 (Untreated and mildly treated mineral oils; highly refined mineral oils are Group 3 — not classifiable)

name: PTFE Dispersion

toxicology.skin_result: Not irritating.
toxicology.stot_result: Inhalation of pyrolysis products (above 300°C) may cause polymer fume fever (flu-like symptoms). Pyrolysis at very high temperatures can produce toxic decomposition products including perfluoroisobutylene.

persistence: PTFE is a fully fluorinated polymer that is extremely chemically stable and essentially non-biodegradable. It is not expected to be degraded by hydrolysis, photolysis, or biological processes under environmental conditions.
bioaccumulation: PTFE is a high molecular weight polymer and is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is essentially insoluble and not bioavailable.
mobility: PTFE is a high molecular weight insoluble polymer. It is not mobile in the environment and is not expected to leach into groundwater.

name: Polyacrylic Acid (Versaflex SI)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: Polyacrylic acid is a synthetic polymer and is not readily biodegradable. It is resistant to microbial degradation under standard test conditions.
bioaccumulation: Due to its high molecular weight and polymeric nature, polyacrylic acid is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: Polyacrylic acid is expected to have low mobility in soil due to its high molecular weight and strong adsorption to soil particles.

name: Propenoic Acid Homopolymer, Sodium Salt

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under standard test conditions.

persistence: Sodium polyacrylate is a synthetic polymer and is not readily biodegradable under standard test conditions. It is expected to be persistent in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its high molecular weight and ionic nature. BCF is not applicable for high-molecular-weight polymers.
mobility: Sodium polyacrylate is a high-molecular-weight anionic polymer with low mobility in soil. It is expected to adsorb strongly to soil particles due to its polyelectrolyte character.

name: Block Copolymer Surfactant

toxicology.skin_result: Non-irritating to slightly irritating to skin.

persistence: Poloxamers (block copolymers of ethylene oxide and propylene oxide) are not readily biodegradable based on standard OECD tests; however, they may undergo slow ultimate biodegradation under environmental conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its high molecular weight and hydrophilic character.
mobility: The substance is expected to be highly mobile in the aquatic environment due to its high water solubility; soil adsorption is low.

name: Sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP)

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: Sodium hexametaphosphate hydrolyzes in aqueous solution to orthophosphate over time and is not considered persistent in the environment. It is not readily biodegradable as a synthetic inorganic polymer, but degrades abiotically via hydrolysis.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. As an inorganic phosphate salt, it has negligible bioaccumulation potential.
mobility: The substance is highly soluble in water and is expected to be mobile in the aquatic environment. Phosphate species may adsorb to sediments and soils.

name: Cobalt Nitrate

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. May cause sensitization by skin contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause damage to organs (lungs) through prolonged or repeated exposure.

persistence: Cobalt nitrate is an inorganic salt that dissociates in water to cobalt(II) ions and nitrate ions. The cobalt ion is a metal ion and not subject to biodegradation. Nitrate is subject to natural biogeochemical cycling. The substance is considered persistent with respect to the cobalt cation.
bioaccumulation: Cobalt ions are not expected to significantly bioaccumulate. BCF values for cobalt are low (BCF < 100). The substance has low bioaccumulation potential.
mobility: Cobalt nitrate is highly water-soluble and dissociates completely in aqueous solution. Cobalt ions are mobile in aquatic environments but may adsorb to soil organic matter and sediments (Koc estimated low to moderate). Highly mobile in water.
iarc_classification: Group 2B (cobalt and cobalt compounds, insoluble; cobalt(II) sulfate and other soluble cobalt(II) salts are Group 2B)
ntp_classification: Reasonably Anticipated to be a Human Carcinogen (cobalt and cobalt compounds)

regulatory.prop_65_warning: Cobalt and cobalt compounds are listed under California Proposition 65 as chemicals known to cause cancer.

name: Sodium Acetate Anhyd

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: Sodium acetate is readily biodegradable. Acetate is rapidly metabolized by microorganisms under aerobic conditions. It is not expected to persist in the environment.
bioaccumulation: Sodium acetate is not expected to bioaccumulate due to its low log Kow and high water solubility.
mobility: Sodium acetate is highly mobile in soil due to its high water solubility and low adsorption to soil particles.

name: Xylene

toxicology.skin_result: Causes skin irritation. Defatting of skin with repeated or prolonged contact.
toxicology.stot_result: May cause drowsiness or dizziness. Repeated exposure may cause central nervous system effects.

persistence: Xylene is readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions. It is expected to biodegrade in the environment. Xylene may also volatilize rapidly from water and soil surfaces due to its relatively high vapor pressure.
bioaccumulation: Xylene has low potential for bioaccumulation (log Kow: 3.12–3.20; estimated BCF: 25–90 L/kg in fish).
mobility: Xylene is moderately mobile in soil (Koc: approximately 240–570 L/kg). It may leach to groundwater but is also subject to volatilization and biodegradation.
iarc_classification: Group 3 (Not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans)

name: Potassium Chloride Cry

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant under GHS criteria.

persistence: Potassium chloride is an inorganic salt and is not subject to biodegradation. It dissociates into potassium and chloride ions in aqueous solution and is considered persistent in the environment; however, it is a naturally occurring substance found ubiquitously in the environment.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate. It is an inorganic ionic compound with no significant log Kow.
mobility: Potassium chloride is highly soluble in water (approximately 340 g/L at 20°C) and dissociates completely into ions. It is highly mobile in soil and aquatic environments.

name: Disodium Phosphate Anhydrous Granular

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation with prolonged contact.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause eye irritation; solutions are alkaline and can cause irritation.

persistence: Inorganic phosphate salt; not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense. Phosphate ions are naturally occurring and participate in biological nutrient cycles. The substance is not considered persistent in the regulatory sense.
bioaccumulation: Inorganic phosphate is not expected to bioaccumulate. Log Kow is not applicable to this inorganic salt.
mobility: Highly soluble in water; phosphate ions are mobile in aquatic environments and may contribute to eutrophication.

name: Monosodium Phosphate Anhydrous

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation upon prolonged or repeated contact.

persistence: Inorganic phosphate salts are not subject to biodegradation in the conventional sense. Phosphate is a naturally occurring nutrient and is mineralized in the environment; it is not considered persistent in the sense of organic pollutants.
bioaccumulation: The substance is inorganic and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: Sodium and phosphate ions are highly mobile in aquatic environments. Phosphate may bind to soils and sediments under certain conditions.

name: Chitosan

toxicology.skin_result: Not a skin irritant based on available data.
toxicology.eye_result: Not a serious eye irritant based on available data.

persistence: Chitosan is a naturally occurring biopolymer derived from chitin and is readily biodegradable in the environment by chitinase-producing microorganisms.
bioaccumulation: Chitosan is a high molecular weight polymer and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: As a high molecular weight polysaccharide, chitosan has low mobility in soil and aquatic environments.

name: Silica powders (Precipitated)

toxicology.skin_result: Non-irritating to skin.
toxicology.eye_result: May cause mechanical irritation to eyes.
toxicology.stot_result: Repeated inhalation exposure may cause lung effects (silicosis not associated with precipitated amorphous silica under normal conditions of use).

persistence: Precipitated amorphous silica is an inorganic mineral substance. Biodegradation is not applicable. The substance is not expected to persist in the environment in the same manner as organic pollutants; it is slowly soluble in water forming silicic acid.
bioaccumulation: The substance is inorganic and is not expected to bioaccumulate in organisms.
mobility: Precipitated amorphous silica is a solid with low solubility in water (~150 mg/L at neutral pH). Mobility in soil is low; the substance is not expected to leach significantly.

name: Tannin Extract

toxicology.skin_result: May cause mild skin irritation.

persistence: Tannin extract (tannic acid) is considered readily biodegradable under aerobic conditions.
bioaccumulation: The substance is not expected to bioaccumulate based on its high molecular weight and hydrophilic character.
mobility: The substance is expected to have low mobility in soil due to adsorption to organic matter and soil particles.

name: Sodium Polyaspartate
